# Quotation, paraphrase and inference

Quotation reproduces a source's words and should be marked with quotation formatting and a precise citation. A paraphrase expresses the same claim in new words and still needs attribution. An inference goes beyond what the source explicitly says; label it as your conclusion and explain the supporting observations.

Do not place an interpretation inside a quotation block. When drafting, keep source excerpts adjacent to their citation and use a separate paragraph for analysis. Agreement with an author does not remove the distinction. A capture date helps a reader understand which version of a changing page was consulted.
